transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. It's as clear as if he’s standing right behind me, like when I'm out on the trail or in my painting room. And even though part of me knows he’s dead... in the moment when it happens, it feels completely real.
Have you heard the voice of anyone other than Garrett?

No, it's just Garrett. Like I said, it's just his voice. It happens when I'm out walking the trail, or sometimes when I'm in my painting room. It's just so clear... like he's right there behind me. I know he passed away, but when I hear it, it just feels so real. I haven't heard anyone else, just him.
How long ago did Garrett die?
It was about a month ago. This whole... crisis, I guess you could call it, has just been unfolding ever since he died.
When you are not hearing Garrett’s voice, do you believe that he is actually present or communicating with you?

No, I don't. When the voice isn't happening, I'm... I'm very aware that he's gone. I don't think his spirit is in the room with me or trying to send me signs or anything like that. It's really just in those specific moments when I actually hear him that it messes with my head and feels real. The rest of the time, I know he's dead.
Aside from hearing Garrett’s voice, have you developed any unusual beliefs that other people would consider implausible or untrue?

No, I don't think so. I haven't had any strange ideas or beliefs like that. It's really just the voice. Everything else... I mean, I know what's real and what isn't, aside from when that happens. So, no, nothing else unusual.
How much has hearing Garrett’s voice interfered with your usual daily activities?

It's interfered a lot. I mean, it got to the point where I couldn't practice safely anymore. I'm a psychologist, so... I had to start canceling my patient sessions. I just couldn't focus on them. I fell completely behind on all my documentation, too. At home, it was bad enough that my wife ended up calling crisis services because I just... I couldn't trust myself to be alone. Coming into the hospital was really the breaking point where everything—my work, my home life, my own safety—just stopped functioning.
Do you hear Garrett’s voice only in places or situations that remind you of him?

No, it's not tied to anything specific like that. I've heard him at work, at home... even when I'm just doing something completely unrelated to him. It doesn't seem to matter where I am or what I'm doing. It just happens.
Have you continued hearing Garrett’s voice for more than one month without it stopping completely?
No, it hasn't been that long. Garrett died about a month ago, and this whole... crisis, I guess, has just been unfolding since then. So it hasn't been more than a month.
Have other people noticed that your speech has become difficult to follow or that you are jumping between unrelated topics?

Yeah, they have. People kept telling me to slow down because I was talking over them. I would jump around a lot—going from my clinical ideas straight to Garrett, and then right into these theater plans. I just... I felt this physical pressure in my chest to keep going. Like I had to get all the words out before they disappeared. So, yes, it was definitely hard for them to follow.
During this period, have you felt unusually elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, definitely. Most of the day, every day. At first, I felt almost lit up... like I had this urgent purpose that no one else could see. But if anyone questioned me, or if they tried to slow me down, I would just snap into a rage. So it was really a mix of both.
During this period, have you needed much less sleep than usual while still feeling rested?

Yes, I did. Um, for weeks I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, and I felt completely wired. Like I didn't need any more than that. But then... I started crashing. Now I fall into this broken, heavy sleep, but it doesn't help. It still leaves me waking up completely exhausted and panicky before dawn.
During this period, have you felt unusually powerful, important, or capable of things that others would consider unrealistic?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I had a lot of ideas and things I wanted to do, like I mentioned with the theater plans and my work, but I didn't think I had superpowers or anything like that. I just felt really driven to get things done, not that I was somehow more important than anyone else.
When you are not feeling unusually energized or irritable, do you still hear Garrett’s voice?

No, I don't. I... I only started hearing Garrett's voice during that whole wired stretch I was telling you about, when I was barely sleeping and taking on all those impossible projects. I felt so driven to just keep going. But I had never heard him like that before my mood shifted that way. It wasn't... it wasn't something that happened during my ordinary grief. It only happened when I was all keyed up.
